decisive_items: The pediatrician made a provisional diagnosis of immune thrombocytopenia and administered intravenous immunoglobulins (2 g/kg) the day before surgery
He had no bleeding history or medications
Prothrombin time, activated partial thromboplastin time, and INR were normal; peripheral smear was unremarkable
response.rationale: Isolated thrombocytopenia with normal coagulation and no secondary infectious or autoimmune cause makes immune thrombocytopenia the most likely new diagnosis; negative antiplatelet antibodies do not exclude ITP. The congenital heart defect is established background rather than the current diagnostic question.

rejected.why: PA/VSD is the pre-existing congenital diagnosis; it does not explain the new isolated thrombocytopenia or the IVIG-based immune workup/management.
